proof:
Source: parent Steps 3–4, the summation of the piecewise co-area formula over the pieces. This is the procedure of Simon Ch. 3: Remark 1.3 (chapter-03.txt ll. 67–72), the proof of 2.4 by summing over j (ll. 378–395), and 2.8–2.9 obtained from the C¹ case "by using the decomposition M = ⋃ M_j of Remark 1.3" (ll. 412–435). It is restated in Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, last part (chapter-06.txt ll. 1156–1183).

Conventions: all integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞]; dt is Lebesgue measure on ℝ; |g(x)| = ‖g x‖ₑ. For A ⊆ ℝ^P and t ∈ ℝ, A_t := A ∩ {g ≠ 0} ∩ f⁻¹(t). Put h_j(t) := ∫_{(S_j)_t} φ dν.

1. Slice decomposition. Fix t ∈ ℝ. We show M_t = ⋃_j (S_j)_t.
 (⊇) If x ∈ (S_j)_t, then x ∈ S_j ⊆ M, g(x) ≠ 0 and f(x) = t, so x ∈ M_t.
 (⊆) Let x ∈ M_t. If x ∉ S_j for every j, the hypothesis on g gives g(x) = 0, which contradicts g(x) ≠ 0. So x ∈ S_j for some j, and then x ∈ (S_j)_t.

2. The slices are measurable and disjoint.
 - {x : g(x) ≠ 0} = g⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ {0}) is Borel, since g is Borel and {0} is closed.
 - f⁻¹({t}) is Borel, since f is Borel and {t} is closed.
 - Hence each (S_j)_t = S_j ∩ {g ≠ 0} ∩ f⁻¹(t) is Borel.
 - For i ≠ j, (S_i)_t ⊆ S_i and (S_j)_t ⊆ S_j, so they are disjoint because S_i and S_j are.

3. The slice integral is a series. The lower integral is countably additive over a countable disjoint family of measurable sets (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion; no measurability of the integrand φ is required). By steps 1–2, for every t:
 ∫_{M_t} φ dν = Σ_j ∫_{(S_j)_t} φ dν = Σ_j h_j(t).
 So the functions t ↦ ∫_{M_t} φ dν and t ↦ Σ_j h_j(t) are equal.

4. A.e.-measurability (first conclusion). Each h_j is a.e.-measurable by hypothesis. A countable sum of a.e.-measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions is a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum, a deprecated alias of AEMeasurable.tsum). By step 3, t ↦ ∫_{M_t} φ dν is a.e.-measurable.

5. Integrating the series. Monotone convergence for series of a.e.-measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions (lintegral_tsum, using the a.e.-measurability of each h_j) gives ∫_ℝ Σ_j h_j(t) dt = Σ_j ∫_ℝ h_j(t) dt. By the piece hypothesis this equals Σ_j ∫_{S_j} |g| φ dμ.

6. The right-hand side is a series. Let G(x) := |g(x)| φ(x).
 - If x ∉ ⋃_j S_j, then g(x) = 0, so G(x) = 0. Hence the support of G lies in ⋃_j S_j ⊆ M.
 - A lower integral over a set containing the support of the integrand equals the integral over the whole space (setLIntegral_eq_of_support_subset). Applied to M and to ⋃_j S_j, this gives ∫_M G dμ = ∫ G dμ = ∫_{⋃_j S_j} G dμ.
 - The S_j are Borel and pairwise disjoint, so countable additivity (lintegral_iUnion) gives ∫_{⋃_j S_j} G dμ = Σ_j ∫_{S_j} G dμ.

7. Conclusion. Steps 3, 5 and 6 give
 ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} φ dν dt = ∫_ℝ Σ_j h_j(t) dt = Σ_j ∫_{S_j} |g| φ dμ = ∫_M |g| φ dμ,
 which is the second conclusion. ∎
key_steps: M_t = ⋃_j (S_j)_t, because g = 0 off ⋃_j S_j and S_j ⊆ M.
The (S_j)_t are Borel and pairwise disjoint, so ∫_{M_t} φ dν = Σ_j h_j(t) for every t (lintegral_iUnion).
A countable sum of a.e.-measurable functions is a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum), giving the first conclusion.
Monotone convergence for series (lintegral_tsum) and the piece hypothesis give ∫_ℝ Σ_j h_j dt = Σ_j ∫_{S_j} |g|φ dμ.
supp(|g|φ) ⊆ ⋃_j S_j ⊆ M, so ∫_M |g|φ dμ = Σ_j ∫_{S_j} |g|φ dμ (setLIntegral_eq_of_support_subset, lintegral_iUnion).
